turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (PATIENT): Sorry I'm late doctor, the luas was after packing up at harcourt and I stood in the rain like an eejit for a good twenty minutes.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): Ah you're grand, come on in. This yoke of a computer is frozen, give me a second here.

[SEG0003] person_1 (PATIENT): No bother. I was only saying to the girl outside that the rain is desperate, and I'd dropped my sister to the train for cork, her fella's people have a christening down there, so the timing went all wrong on me.
[SEG0004] person_2 (DOCTOR): Mm. Right. Sorry, I had the wrong chart open. What was that about your sister?
[SEG0005] person_1 (PATIENT): Just that she's away to cork, nothing to do with me really. I suppose I should get to why I came.
[SEG0006] person_1 (PATIENT): Well I've been seizure free two years now on the tablets, and I wanted to ask you about the driving, whether I'm allowed back behind the wheel.
[SEG0007] person_2 (DOCTOR): The driving. Ok let me find the epilepsy letter. Two years, you said?

[SEG0008] person_1 (PATIENT): Yes, two years. The last proper one was in the kitchen, I went down on the floor, that was march two years ago, and nothing like that since. I've been really really careful with the tablets and the sleep and all of it.
[SEG0009] person_2 (DOCTOR): Sorry, march two years ago? Say it again, the screen just jumped on me.
[SEG0010] person_1 (PATIENT): March, two years back. Seizure free since then. That's what I was hoping would be enough for the licence.
[SEG0011] person_2 (DOCTOR): And the medicine is still the levetiracetam?

[SEG0012] person_1 (PATIENT): Yes, the levetirasetam, five hundred milligrams in the morning and five hundred at night. White tablets, from the chemist on camden street, I've been on that dose a good while now.
[SEG0013] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any seizures at all since, or any blank spells, even short ones?
[SEG0014] person_1 (PATIENT): No. No, nothing at all. Not a blank spell, not a twitch. I would have known, I'm very tuned in to it after all these years.
[SEG0015] person_2 (DOCTOR): Good. Sorry, the dose again? I think I typed four hundred.
[SEG0016] person_1 (PATIENT): Five hundred. Twice a day. I never miss them at home, the phone alarm goes off and I take them with breakfast and with the tea.

[SEG0017] person_1 (PATIENT): I should say though, I was in spain for ten days last month and it all went sideways. The tablets ended up in the hold, the time difference threw me, and I missed the morning dose two days for certain, maybe a third morning, I genuinely can't remember if it was two or three. I got all the evening ones into me.
[SEG0018] person_2 (DOCTOR): Missed mornings in spain. Right, hold on while this saves. Did you feel off after the missed ones?

[SEG0019] person_1 (PATIENT): I thought I was grand. But umm, my brother paul came for dinner the week I got home and he said I went blank, stopped mid sentence and stared at the wall. He reckoned a few seconds, about ten, and then I carried on, and I had no memory of it myself. I've been going back and forth on whether to even mention it.
[SEG0020] person_2 (DOCTOR): You went blank. Sorry, how long did he say? I was reading the old letter.

[SEG0021] person_1 (PATIENT): About ten seconds. No falling down, no shaking, I didn't bite my tongue. He was very sure and he's not a fella who makes things up, we were halfway through the beef stew talking about the match. I told him at the time he imagined it but looking back I think he was right.
[SEG0022] person_2 (DOCTOR): And when exactly was this dinner?

[SEG0023] person_1 (PATIENT): Last month, the week I got back from spain. I can't pin the date, it was a thursday or a friday I think, err, somewhere in the middle of the month, and I've gone over the calendar and I still can't settle it.
[SEG0024] person_2 (DOCTOR): Ok. Any headache with it, or any weakness in an arm or a leg afterwards?
[SEG0025] person_1 (PATIENT): No headache, and no weakness. I was a bit tired after but I put that down to the flight and two glasses of wine with the dinner, nothing more than that.
[SEG0026] person_2 (DOCTOR): Right. I'm calling that a possible small seizure, an absence, maybe from the missed tablets. I can't say you're fit to drive on the back of it.

[SEG0027] person_1 (PATIENT): I was afraid you'd say that. I had the ndls form half filled, I even rang them and the woman was lovely but she said it has to be the doctor who signs it. The bus from drumcondra to the office in rathmines is an hour and a quarter and my boss is already giving out about the late mornings.
[SEG0028] person_2 (DOCTOR): I hear you. What we'll do is a blood test, a levetiracetam level, so we can see if the level is where it should be. I'll have that booked.

[SEG0029] person_1 (PATIENT): A blood test, grand. Do I need to fast, because if it's early morning the bus is a nightmare and I'd have to shift a whole meeting, and last time the queue here was forty minutes and I missed the start of one.
[SEG0030] person_2 (DOCTOR): No fasting. Any time this week. Reception will give you the form on the way out. Sorry, you said 500 twice a day, yes?
[SEG0031] person_1 (PATIENT): Yes, 500 twice a day. I'll come thursday morning if I can get in before nine, otherwise friday, depending on that meeting my boss moved.
[SEG0032] person_2 (DOCTOR): Fine. Until that result is back, and until we've looked at this properly, no driving. Not even down the road.

[SEG0033] person_1 (PATIENT): Understood. I'll stay on the bus. I'd rather be sure than have something happen, especially with the school traffic near the office, though they're not my children, I don't have kids, it's just the crossing is busy.

[SEG0034] person_2 (DOCTOR): Good. Keep the levetiracetam exactly as it is, morning and night, and don't miss any. I'll see you back here in two weeks and we'll go through the level and the driving then.

[SEG0035] person_1 (PATIENT): Two weeks, yes. I'll set the alarm properly this time, it didn't go off in spain, either the roaming or I had it on silent, I still don't know which. Is there anything else you need me to bring?
[SEG0036] person_2 (DOCTOR): No, that's everything. Bloods this week, back in two weeks. Mind yourself, it's still pouring out there.

spec.situation: Adult with epilepsy on levetiracetam, seizure-free for two years, asks about driving; missed doses when travelling; relative saw a 'blank spell' last month; doctor reviews and plans a blood test.

traps.happens: The conversation OPENS with a remark, joke, apology for being late, small talk, or a trigger event (a relative's diagnosis, a neighbour's advice, the receptionist's note) BEFORE the real reason is stated. The patient states the real concern a few turns later.
traps.label_rule: chief_complaint is the real concern in a short phrase in the patient's wording (e.g. 'worried about diabetes', 'voice gets tired'). NOT the opening remark, the joke or the trigger (the relative's illness goes into family_history only if it is a relative's condition said as such).

features: denial_then_admission: the patient first denies a symptom, then later describes it. The label records the symptom as present (the later, fuller answer) and does NOT also record the earlier denial as a negative finding.
doctor_misses_topics: the doctor does not ask about everything; topics never discussed are simply absent (no invented denials, no allergy line if allergies were never mentioned).
spec.doctor_style: distracted by the computer, asks for repeats

bad.reason: Drumcondra is mentioned for bus route, but living there is not explicitly stated.
Blank spell lasted about 10 seconds last month, but frequency once and certainty certain are not fully established.
bad.text: blank spell (category=neurological, status=present, duration=approximately 10 seconds, frequency=once, onset=last month, temporality=past, reported_by=patient, certainty=certain)

bad.reason: Past seizure history supported, but 'resolved' and onset exactly two years ago are not stated; last proper seizure was March two years ago.
bad.text: seizure (category=neurological, status=resolved, onset=two years ago, temporality=past, reported_by=patient, certainty=certain)

omissions.text: Patient reported no seizures at all since March two years ago and specifically denied any further blank spells or twitches until the possible event last month.
Last proper seizure was in March two years ago, when the patient collapsed in the kitchen and went down on the floor.
Medication adherence detail: patient takes levetiracetam 500 mg with breakfast and with tea and says they never miss doses at home using a phone alarm.

Recent nonadherence detail: while in Spain for 10 days last month, levetiracetam was packed in the hold and the patient missed the morning dose on two days for certain, possibly a third, but took all evening doses.
The blank spell was witnessed by the patient's brother Paul after return from Spain; the patient had no memory of it and initially thought the brother imagined it.
Key negative features of the possible seizure were denied: no fall, no shaking, and no tongue biting.
Patient reported being a bit tired afterwards, which they attributed to the flight and two glasses of wine with dinner.

Doctor advised no driving 'not even down the road' until the result is back and the event has been properly reviewed; doctor explicitly said they could not say the patient was fit to drive because of this possible small seizure.
Blood test instruction: no fasting is required and it can be done any time this week; reception will provide the form on the way out.
